verses.text: Then Bildad the Shuhite replied:

xrefs.text: Now when Job’s three friends— Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite— heard about all this adversity that had come upon him, each of them came from his home, and they met together to go and sympathize with Job and comfort him.
Then Bildad the Shuhite replied:

After the LORD had spoken these words to Job, He said to Eliphaz the Temanite, “My wrath is kindled against you and your two friends. For you have not spoken about Me accurately, as My servant Job has.
Then Bildad the Shuhite replied:

verses.text: “How long until you end these speeches? Show some sense, and then we can talk.

xrefs.text: If only you would remain silent; for that would be your wisdom!
He who answers a matter before he hears it— this is folly and disgrace to him.
“How long will you go on saying such things? The words of your mouth are a blustering wind.
[“]But now, O Job, hear my speech, and listen to all my words.
“Listen carefully to my words; let this be your consolation to me.

verses.text: Why are we regarded as cattle, as stupid in your sight?

xrefs.text: I was senseless and ignorant; I was a brute beast before You.
You have closed their minds to understanding; therefore You will not exalt them.
But come back and try again, all of you. For I will not find a wise man among you.
Be devoted to one another in brotherly love. Outdo yourselves in honoring one another.
I said to myself, “As for the sons of men, God tests them so that they may see for themselves that they are but beasts.”

verses.text: You who tear yourself in anger— should the earth be forsaken on your account, or the rocks be moved from their place?

xrefs.text: But as a mountain erodes and crumbles and a rock is dislodged from its place,
His anger has torn me and opposed me; He gnashes His teeth at me. My adversary pierces me with His eyes.
For resentment kills a fool, and envy slays the simple.
Why do I put myself at risk and take my life in my own hands?
Would you really annul My justice? Would you condemn Me to justify yourself?

verses.text: Indeed, the lamp of the wicked is extinguished; the flame of his fire does not glow.

xrefs.text: The light of the righteous shines brightly, but the lamp of the wicked is extinguished.
Whoever curses his father or mother, his lamp will be extinguished in deepest darkness.
For the evil man has no future; the lamp of the wicked will be extinguished.
How often is the lamp of the wicked put out? Does disaster come upon them? Does God, in His anger, apportion destruction?
But the way of the wicked is like the darkest gloom; they do not know what makes them stumble.

verses.text: The light in his tent grows dark, and the lamp beside him goes out.

xrefs.text: The light of a lamp will never shine in you again, and the voices of a bride and bridegroom will never call out in you again. For your merchants were the great ones of the earth, because all the nations were deceived by your sorcery.
For You, O LORD, light my lamp; my God lights up my darkness.
How often is the lamp of the wicked put out? Does disaster come upon them? Does God, in His anger, apportion destruction?

verses.text: His vigorous stride is shortened, and his own schemes trip him up.

xrefs.text: When you walk, your steps will not be impeded; when you run, you will not stumble.
The LORD frustrates the plans of the nations; He thwarts the devices of the peoples.
You broaden the path beneath me so that my ankles do not give way.
For the wisdom of this world is foolishness in God’s sight. As it is written: “He catches the wise in their craftiness.”
Your own mouth, not mine, condemns you; your own lips testify against you.

verses.text: For his own feet lead him into a net, and he wanders into its mesh.

xrefs.text: The nations have fallen into a pit of their making; their feet are caught in the net they have hidden.
May ruin befall them by surprise; may the net they hid ensnare them; may they fall into the hazard they created.
Therefore snares surround you, and sudden peril terrifies you;
Then King Xerxes spoke up and asked Queen Esther, “Who is this, and where is the one who would devise such a scheme?”
An evil man is caught by his own sin, but a righteous one sings and rejoices.

verses.text: A trap seizes his heel; a snare grips him.

xrefs.text: The hungry consume his harvest, taking it even from the thorns, and the thirsty pant after his wealth.

And He will be a sanctuary— but to both houses of Israel a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense, to the dwellers of Jerusalem a trap and a snare.

While he was still speaking, another messenger came and reported: “The Chaldeans formed three bands, raided the camels, and took them away. They put the servants to the sword, and I alone have escaped to tell you!”

verses.text: A noose is hidden in the ground, and a trap lies in his path.

xrefs.text: But I will spread My net over him, and he will be caught in My snare. I will bring him to Babylon, the land of the Chaldeans; yet he will not see it, and there he will die.
On the wicked He will rain down fiery coals and sulfur; a scorching wind will be their portion.
And David says: “May their table become a snare and a trap, a stumbling block and a retribution to them.

verses.text: Terrors frighten him on every side and harass his every step.

xrefs.text: Sounds of terror fill his ears; in his prosperity the destroyer attacks him.
Do not go out to the fields; do not walk the road. For the enemy has a sword; terror is on every side.
Why am I seeing this? They are terrified, they are retreating; their warriors are defeated, they flee in haste without looking back; terror is on every side!” declares the LORD.

As for those of you who survive, I will send a faintness into their hearts in the lands of their enemies, so that even the sound of a windblown leaf will put them to flight. And they will flee as one flees the sword, and fall when no one pursues them.
They will take their tents and flocks, their tent curtains and all their goods. They will take their camels for themselves. They will shout to them: ‘Terror is on every side!’

verses.text: His strength is depleted, and calamity is ready at his side.

xrefs.text: He wanders about as food for vultures; he knows the day of darkness is at hand.
They will roam the land, dejected and hungry. When they are famished, they will become enraged; and looking upward, they will curse their king and their God.
In their greed, these false teachers will exploit you with deceptive words. The longstanding verdict against them remains in force, and their destruction does not sleep.
May his children wander as beggars, seeking sustenance far from their ruined homes.
Young lions go lacking and hungry, but those who seek the LORD lack no good thing.

verses.text: It devours patches of his skin; the firstborn of death devours his limbs.

xrefs.text: Then the firstborn of the poor will find pasture, and the needy will lie down in safety, but I will kill your root by famine, and your remnant will be slain.
To the roots of the mountains I descended; the earth beneath me barred me in forever! But You raised my life from the pit, O LORD my God!
Will it go down to the gates of Sheol? Will we go down together into the dust?”

And this will be the plague with which the LORD strikes all the peoples who have warred against Jerusalem: Their flesh will rot while they stand on their feet, their eyes will rot in their sockets, and their tongues will rot in their mouths.

Then I looked and saw a pale green horse. Its rider’s name was Death, and Hades followed close behind. And they were given authority over a fourth of the earth, to kill by sword, by famine, by plague, and by the beasts of the earth.

verses.text: He is torn from the shelter of his tent and is marched off to the king of terrors.

xrefs.text: The hope of the righteous is joy, but the expectations of the wicked will perish.
But everyone who hears these words of Mine and does not act on them is like a foolish man who built his house on sand.
The wicked man will see and be grieved; he will gnash his teeth and waste away; the desires of the wicked will perish.
The wicked man is thrown down by his own sin, but the righteous man has a refuge even in death.

verses.text: Fire resides in his tent; burning sulfur rains down on his dwelling.

xrefs.text: On the wicked He will rain down fiery coals and sulfur; a scorching wind will be their portion.
Edom’s streams will be turned to tar, and her soil to sulfur; her land will become a blazing pitch.

All its soil will be a burning waste of sulfur and salt, unsown and unproductive, with no plant growing on it, just like the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim, which the LORD overthrew in His fierce anger.

But to the cowardly and unbelieving and abominable and murderers and sexually immoral and sorcerers and idolaters and all liars, their place will be in the lake that burns with fire and sulfur. This is the second death.
He must return the fruit of his labor without consuming it; he cannot enjoy the profits of his trading.

verses.text: The roots beneath him dry up, and the branches above him wither away.

xrefs.text: Ephraim is struck down; their root is withered; they cannot bear fruit. Even if they bear children, I will slay the darlings of their wombs.

Therefore, as a tongue of fire consumes the straw, and as dry grass shrivels in the flame, so their roots will decay and their blossoms will blow away like dust; for they have rejected the instruction of the LORD of Hosts and despised the word of the Holy One of Israel.
He will not escape from the darkness; the flame will wither his shoots, and the breath of God’s mouth will carry him away.

“For behold, the day is coming, burning like a furnace, when all the arrogant and every evildoer will be stubble; the day is coming when I will set them ablaze,” says the LORD of Hosts. “Not a root or branch will be left to them.”
Yet it was I who destroyed the Amorite before them, though his height was like that of the cedars, and he was as strong as the oaks. Yet I destroyed his fruit above and his roots below.

verses.text: The memory of him perishes from the earth, and he has no name in the land.

xrefs.text: But the face of the LORD is against those who do evil, to wipe out all memory of them from the earth.
The memory of the righteous is a blessing, but the name of the wicked will rot.
May his descendants be cut off; may their name be blotted out from the next generation.
but the wicked will be cut off from the land, and the unfaithful will be uprooted.
Your maxims are proverbs of ashes; your defenses are defenses of clay.

verses.text: He is driven from light into darkness and is chased from the inhabited world.

xrefs.text: He will fly away like a dream, never to be found; he will be chased away like a vision in the night.

At that moment the sentence against Nebuchadnezzar was fulfilled. He was driven away from mankind. He ate grass like an ox, and his body was drenched with the dew of heaven, until his hair grew like the feathers of an eagle and his nails like the claws of a bird.
The nations rage like the rush of many waters. He rebukes them, and they flee far away, driven before the wind like chaff on the hills, like tumbleweeds before a gale.

verses.text: He has no offspring or posterity among his people, no survivor where he once lived.

xrefs.text: This is what the LORD says: “Enroll this man as childless, a man who will not prosper in his lifetime. None of his descendants will prosper to sit on the throne of David or to rule again in Judah.”
Prepare a place to slaughter his sons for the iniquities of their forefathers. They will never rise up to possess a land or cover the earth with their cities.
May his descendants be cut off; may their name be blotted out from the next generation.
Woe to you who add house to house and join field to field until no place is left and you live alone in the land.
Total darkness is reserved for his treasures. A fire unfanned will consume him and devour what is left in his tent.

verses.text: Those in the west are appalled at his fate, while those in the east tremble in horror.

Kill all her young bulls; let them go down to the slaughter. Woe to them, for their day has come— the time of their punishment.
They have made their land a desolation, a perpetual object of scorn; all who pass by will be appalled and shake their heads.

They profess to know God, but by their actions they deny Him. They are detestable, disobedient, and unfit for any good deed.
